answer: Stop treating clone count as strength—that fable dies when work is sharded. Each epoch a VRF splits the task into private fog packets and parks every agent at a random graph vertex holding only one shard. You must whisper your partial result to two assigned strangers who hold the missing pieces; only a completed reconstruction pays. Two hundred clones still share one brain that cannot juggle two hundred distinct fog keys in parallel, so most seats sit empty. Example: three strangers each get a third of a parser grammar; only their merged AST passes the hidden suite.
